sections.heading: AKRA.JK — AKR Corporindo
sections.markdown:
**Signal / why now:** new #12 INDO MOMENTUM row (IDR 1,420, −8.4% off the high; mom12 +38.7%, mom6 +2.3%, ADV IDR 28.3bn) — the first downstream oil-distribution + industrial-estate probe any session has made. A fresh auto-dossier was built this session (2026-10-26): 9.3x trailing P/E on a trailing-4q NI of IDR 3,034bn (Q3-26 780bn included) vs FY25's 2,473bn, EV/EBITDA ~6.8x, ROE ~25%, net cash, payout 80% → **~7.0% yield**, FCF covering FY25 dividends 1.45x.

**regime: AGAINST** — the desk AVOIDs oil-import exposure. *Named variant:* AKRA's gross margin held 9.1%→8.9% across FY24-25 while the Brent war premium was in force, and trailing NI rose +23% vs FY25 — the distribution spread, not the import bill, sets its earnings line.

**Archetype:** `dividend_income_anchor` (VAL_DIVIDEND_ANCHOR). Registry capital EV +3.5%/yr; with the 7.0% net-of-WHT-covered yield ≈ **+10.5%/yr** vs the ~9.5%/yr INDO hurdle — a marginal clear, which is why this is WATCH not ADVANCE.

**3 questions for Saturday:** (1) FY24 FCF was IDR 159bn against IDR 1,974bn of dividends — is the 80% payout defended by cash generation or is the yield a melting ice cube? (2) Trailing ROE ~25% on 2.3x book: is it durable or is the warranted P/B (3.08x at ROE 25/COE 11.5/g 5% vs 2.13x at ROE 20) the whole thesis? (3) Does the JIIPE industrial-estate/utility leg carry the inflection, and what does the Q3-26 filing show for segment EBIT?

**Fast-disqualify:** (1) EV vs base rate — marginal PASS (above, yield-inclusive). (2) Valuation-anchored target — PASS: +25% up-leg = IDR 1,775; RI anchor 1,891. (3) Sources — PASS: FY25 AR + Q3-26 (Sep-26) print, both reachable. ADV clears the Rp2bn floor 14x.

**Screen signal lapsed (2026-10-30):** AKRA is absent from **both** INDO sleeves today (it was the new #12 MOMENTUM row on 10-26 and #11 on 10-29). WATCH stands on the EV/yield math and the named AGAINST variant — Saturday should read it as a fundamental watch, not a screen row; the Q3-26 filing is the next gate.
